exercise.name: Sissy Squat

reference.title: Sissy Squat Bodyweight
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Thighs, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

equipment: Wall or sturdy support for one hand

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you come back up.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, short pause, about 1.4 s up

prescription.progression: Deeper range, slower lowering, then hold a light dumbbell or plate at the chest with the free hand.

cues.text: Stand tall on the balls of the feet, feet hip width, left hand resting on a wall beside you.
Breathe in and drive the knees forward and down while the body leans back in one straight line from knees to shoulders.
Go only as deep as the knees allow comfortably; hips stay straight, heels stay up.
Breathe out and pull the knees back under you to stand tall.
Stand tall on the balls of the feet and reset.

mistakes.mistake: Bending at the hips (turning it into a squat)
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and keep the hips straight; lean back instead.
Use the hand for balance only.

mistakes.mistake: Going deeper than the knees tolerate
mistakes.fix: Start with a short range and build depth over weeks.
Stay up on the balls of the feet the whole set.

kinematics.norm: Feet about hip width, on the balls of the feet (reference movement; clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees or more at the bottom as tolerated (clinical opinion); Lee 2022 used about 90 degrees for an upright, knee-dominant squat
Hips stay extended (about 0 degrees or slight extension), unlike a normal squat (clinical opinion)
Leaning back in line with the thighs (clinical opinion)
Knees travel well in front of the toes; restricting this changes hip and knee demand (Fry 2003)
About 2 s down, 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #148912, Sissy Squat Bodyweight, video (movement reference)
Lee, Kim, Heo, Park & Chang 2022, differences in the muscle activities of the quadriceps femoris and hamstrings while performing various squat exercises (BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil 14:12)
Fry, Smith & Schilling 2003, effect of knee position on hip and knee torques during the barbell squat (J Strength Cond Res 17(4):629-633)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Work in a range you can control; add load only once the bodyweight version is smooth.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Knee-dominant: skip it with current knee pain; build depth gradually.
modify: Balance: hold the support with both hands.
regressions: Spanish squat with a band behind the knees.
progressions: Hold a light plate at the chest.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Knee extensors take almost all the load because the hips stay straight and the knees travel far forward. In a squat that kept the trunk and shins upright with the knee at about 90 degrees (Spanish squat), rectus femoris activity was much higher than in a general or wall squat (Lee 2022). Letting the knees travel forward shifts the demand toward the knee (Fry 2003 studied restricted vs unrestricted knee travel).

In a squat that kept the trunk and shins upright with the knee at about 90 degrees (Spanish squat), rectus femoris activity was much higher than in a general or wall squat (Lee 2022). Letting the knees travel forward shifts the demand toward the knee (Fry 2003 studied restricted vs unrestricted knee travel).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Hold the heels up and steady the ankles on the balls of the feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Hold the heels up and steady the ankles on the balls of the feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Rectus femoris crosses the hip and works hard with the hip held extended (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Rectus femoris crosses the hip and works hard with the hip held extended (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps a straight line from the knees to the shoulders as the body leans back (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Holds the hips extended so the body does not fold at the hips (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Holds the hips extended so the body does not fold at the hips (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the trunk long while leaning back (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the trunk long while leaning back (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Steady the trunk against the one-hand support (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Steady the trunk against the one-hand support (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: The hand on the wall only balances; it does not pull (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: The hand on the wall only balances; it does not pull (clinical opinion).
